title: Building the data pipeline
goals: Build a small pipeline from tested parts

prerequisite.prompt: What are the steps between raw records and a recommendation?
prerequisite.answer: Validate, filter eligibility, calculate scores, resolve ties, then report with limits.

vocabulary: One part of a processing pipeline
A function that decides whether an input meets a schema
Keeping different responsibilities in distinct parts
An explanation of why a record was not accepted

blocks.text: Build the validation stage of the planned chooser first. A valid record has nonempty text name, integer minutes 0 through 60 and integer fun and learning ratings 0 through 5. The batch stage must separately check name uniqueness. Only accepted records may reach the Week 24 selection function.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The worked calls print True then False. Short-circuit checks keep absent or wrongly typed fields away from later operations. This Boolean helper does not explain the reason; add reason codes in the reporting stage or use a validation result record. Do not describe a range failure as a no-match outcome.

blocks.label: Predict validity for minutes 0, fun 0, learning 5 with name A, then for minutes 61.

blocks.text: Calling the selector on raw data can crash or produce a result from invalid ratings. Route data through validation first. Duplicate names require a batch check even when each row individually passes; block the ambiguous batch for review instead of arbitrarily keeping one.

Each stage should have a clear input and output contract. A program can be correct at one stage but wrong at their connection, such as passing rejected rows into selection. Keep acceptance and rejection counts in the report.

blocks.label: Two valid rows have the same name but different ratings. Should individual validation alone permit selection?

workbook.title: Trace a validation
workbook.prompt: Explain why a row with fun "4" fails while fun 4 can pass.
workbook.answer: The first is text; the schema requires an exact integer rating from 0 to 5.

workbook.title: Check missing fields
workbook.prompt: What does valid_item return if learning is absent?
workbook.answer: False: get returns None and the exact integer check fails.

workbook.title: Repair the connection
workbook.prompt: A program validates rows but still sends the original raw list to recommend. What should change?
workbook.answer: Pass only the accepted, uniqueness-checked list. Preserve rejection information separately for reporting.

workbook.title: Build independently
workbook.prompt: Combine validation and the Week 24 selector for A (minutes 10, fun 3, learning 2), B (12,4,1), and C (8,"5",5), limit 10. State accepted rows, rejected row, selection and explanation.
workbook.answer: A and B validate; C fails fun type. B exceeds the limit. A wins with score 8. Report 2 accepted of 3, one rejection and one eligible item. Verify unique names.

workbook.title: Handle duplicates
workbook.prompt: Two valid rows have the same name but different ratings. Should individual validation alone permit selection?
workbook.answer: No. The batch uniqueness contract fails. Block the ambiguous batch and report duplicate names for correction.

teacher.background: Teach Week 32 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. Build the validation stage of the planned chooser first. A valid record has nonempty text name, integer minutes 0 through 60 and integer fun and learning ratings 0 through 5. The batch stage must separately check name uniqueness. Only accepted records may reach the Week 24 selection function. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: The first passes. Replacing minutes with 61 fails the range. Exit: No. The batch uniqueness contract fails. Block the ambiguous batch and report duplicate names for correction.
